deep.reconstruction:
Context. The previous page holds Gauss's crystallographic notes, including his axonometry condition t^2+t'^2+t''^2=0. This page treats the cubic holohedral forms whose faces are planes p x + q y + r z = 1. The triple (p,q,r) is any permutation, with any signs, of three non-negative numbers (alpha,beta,gamma). In modern terms these are Miller-type indices, reciprocal intercepts, of the form {hkl}.

(a) Figures. Two sketches show one octant of the hexakisoctahedron, looking down the body diagonal. Each of the six triangles in the octant is labelled by the permutation (p,q,r) giving its plane. Vertex 1 lies on the x-axis (4-fold axis). Vertex 2 lies on the xy face-diagonal (2-fold axis). Vertex 3 lies on the body diagonal (3-fold axis).
- Left figure: ordered alpha>beta>gamma.
- Right figure: ordered alpha<beta<gamma. The first '<' was written as '>' and crossed out.

(b) Coordinates of the three vertices of the fundamental face triangle.
- Left convention:
  - 1 = (1/alpha, 0, 0)
  - 2 = (1/(alpha+beta), 1/(alpha+beta), 0)
  - 3 = (1,1,1)/(alpha+beta+gamma)
- Right convention (the one used for all later formulas):
  - 1 = (1/gamma, 0, 0)
  - 2 = (1/(beta+gamma))(1,1,0)
  - 3 = (1,1,1)/s, with s = alpha+beta+gamma
- Check (mine): the plane gamma x + beta y + alpha z = 1 passes through all three points. On each symmetry axis the maximum over all permuted planes equals 1, so these are genuine vertices of the convex form.

(c) 'Vorkommende Werthe': the index triples actually observed in nature, written in ascending order to match the right-hand convention.
- 001 cube
- 011 rhombic dodecahedron
- 012 tetrakis hexahedron
- 111 octahedron
- 112 trapezoidal icositetrahedron
- 122 triakis octahedron
- 123 hexakisoctahedron
- 133 and 233, also triakis octahedra
- Unnamed: 013, 023, 113, 124, 135, 234(?), 3.5.11
- These are exactly the modern names for {100}, {110}, {210}, {111}, {211}, {221}, {321}, {331}, {332}.
- The marginal numbers (7,3,6,1,5,2,4,2,2) are of unclear meaning; possibly a frequency or order ranking.

(d) Metric quantities, in the right convention.
- Six times the volume of the elementary pyramid (apex at the origin, base triangle 123):
  - 6V = |det(v1,v2,v3)|.
  - The matrix is lower triangular, so 6V = (1/gamma)(1/(beta+gamma))(1/s), as Gauss writes.
- All faces lie at the same distance 1/sqrt(alpha^2+beta^2+gamma^2) from the centre. Hence all these forms are circumscribed about a sphere of that radius.
- Twice the triangle area: 2A = 6V divided by that distance (step mine) = sqrt(alpha^2+beta^2+gamma^2)/(gamma(beta+gamma)s).
- Edge lengths:
  - |12| = sqrt(beta^2+gamma^2)/(gamma(beta+gamma))
  - |13| = sqrt((alpha+beta)^2+2gamma^2)/(gamma s)
  - |23| = sqrt(2alpha^2+(beta+gamma)^2)/((beta+gamma)s)
- Plane angle at vertex 1 between edges 1-3 and 1-2:
  - cos = (alpha beta+beta^2+gamma^2)/sqrt((beta^2+gamma^2)((alpha+beta)^2+2gamma^2))
  - The dot product is (beta(alpha+beta)+gamma^2)/(gamma^2(beta+gamma)s).
- Sine of that angle:
  - The numerator of 1-cos^2 simplifies to gamma^2(alpha^2+beta^2+gamma^2) (step mine).
  - So sin = gamma sqrt(alpha^2+beta^2+gamma^2)/sqrt(...).
  - This agrees with 2A = |12||13| sin.
errors: The sine numerator is written as what looks like a radical over gamma, read as sqrt(gamma), but the correct factor is gamma. Most likely Gauss intended sqrt(gamma gamma) and the radical covers 'γγ'. If it really is sqrt(gamma), it is a slip; the cross-check via 2A = |12||13| sin requires gamma.
No other errors. The coordinates, volume, inradius, area, three edge lengths and the cosine all verify.
The formulas silently assume the right-hand ordering alpha<beta<gamma. This is consistent with the ascending index list, but the left figure's coordinates use the opposite ordering.
The meaning of the marginal numerals beside the list is unexplained; this is not an error, just undetermined.

results.what: Description of cubic crystal forms by face planes px+qy+rz=1 with (p,q,r) a signed permutation of (alpha,beta,gamma), i.e. reciprocal-intercept indices; identification of the observed forms 001, 011, 012, 111, 112, 122, 123, 133, 233 with cube, rhombic dodecahedron, tetrahexahedron, octahedron, trapezohedron, trisoctahedron and hexakisoctahedron.
results.modern_name: Miller indices {hkl} and the forms of the cubic holohedral class m-3m
results.usually_credited_to: Whewell (1825), Grassmann (1829), W. H. Miller (1839); form names from Weiss/Mohs/Naumann

results.what: Vertex coordinates of the hexakisoctahedron {hkl} on the 4-, 2- and 3-fold axes: (1/gamma,0,0), (1,1,0)/(beta+gamma), (1,1,1)/(alpha+beta+gamma).
results.modern_name: Vertices of the dual (Catalan) polyhedron of type {hkl}

results.what: 6V = 1/(gamma(beta+gamma)(alpha+beta+gamma)); insphere radius 1/sqrt(alpha^2+beta^2+gamma^2); doubled face area; three edge lengths; cosine and sine of the face angle at the 4-fold vertex.
results.modern_name: Metric data of the general cubic form {hkl}

deep.surprise_reason: Routine analytic geometry of cubic crystal forms. Gauss's crystallographic Nachlass, including his use of reciprocal-intercept indices and the axonometry theorem on the previous page, is already partly published in Werke and discussed in the literature. Using Miller-type indices around 1830 is of mild historical interest only.

checkable.sympy: a,b,c=symbols('a b c',positive=True); s=a+b+c; v1=Matrix([1/c,0,0]); v2=Matrix([1/(b+c),1/(b+c),0]); v3=Matrix([1,1,1])/s; simplify(Matrix.hstack(v1,v2,v3).det()-1/(c*(b+c)*s))
checkable.asserts: Six times the elementary pyramid volume equals 1/(gamma(beta+gamma)(alpha+beta+gamma)); result 0
All three vertices lie on the face plane gamma x+beta y+alpha z=1; all entries 0
Cosine of the face angle at vertex 1; result 0
1-cos^2 numerator equals gamma^2(alpha^2+beta^2+gamma^2), so the sine factor is gamma, not sqrt(gamma); result 0
Distance from the origin to every face plane is 1/sqrt(alpha^2+beta^2+gamma^2), i.e. the forms have an insphere; result 0

transcription_corrections: Sine formula: the first factor is probably sqrt(gamma*gamma) (= gamma), not sqrt(gamma); the radical appears to cover 'γγ'. Mathematically it must be gamma.
Right-figure condition: 'α [-<-] β < γ' — the deleted first sign was a '>' corrected to '<', giving α<β<γ.
After 'Kante 1.2 =' there is a struck-through symbol before the fraction; it should be ignored.
'[-Id-] pqr' is a small sketch of a face labelled pqr, preceded by a deleted word, introducing the plane equation px+qy+rz=1.
In the figures, vertex labels '1' (on the x-axis), '2' (bottom edge, on the xy diagonal) and '3' (centre, body diagonal) belong to the drawing.
The marginal numerals 7,3,6,1,5,2,4,2,2 are separate annotations, as is '2 —' before 1.3.3. Also separate are a '?' after '2.3.4)' and a smaller added line '3.5.11'.
The top-left 'Sih' is an uncertain reading of a sorting or archival mark.
